title: A Lemon Ice at the Street Fair
subtheme: A Lemon Ice at the Street Fair
description: A cold lemon treat comes in a cup at a neighborhood fair.
cardDescription: A cold lemon treat comes in a cup at a neighborhood fair.
focus: The setting is a Lemon Ice at the Street Fair. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Yellow citrus fruit commonly used for a sharp juice
Utensil with a small bowl at one end
Tart in taste, like a lemon
Support that holds an object upright
Community event with exhibits, contests, and entertainment

answerNotes.ICE: Ice is solid water. It absorbs heat as it melts, which helps cool a drink.
answerNotes.LEMON: Lemon juice is sour. Zest is the thin colored outer peel used for flavor, not the thick white layer beneath it.
answerNotes.CUP: Cup can name a drinking vessel or a measuring amount. A recipe's measured cup is not simply any small mug.
answerNotes.SPOON: A spoon has a small bowl at one end. It can hold liquid, unlike the prongs of a fork.
answerNotes.SWEET: Sweet describes flavor, not temperature or texture. A food can be sweet and cold, or sweet and warm.
answerNotes.SUMMER: Summer scenes use familiar warm-weather outings. Actual temperatures and traditions differ between regions and families.

Large soft covering used for warmth

Applaud by striking the hands together

answerNotes.BAND: Band can mean a strap or a group of musicians. A watch scene uses the strap meaning; an outdoor concert uses the musical group.
answerNotes.MUSIC: Music can be played by instruments or sung. A concert is an event at which music is performed, rather than the music itself.
answerNotes.CHAIR: A chair is intended for one sitter. A bench or sofa generally provides room for more than one person.
answerNotes.BLANKET: A blanket is a covering used for warmth. A quilt usually has several layers held together with stitching.
answerNotes.SONG: A song has words and a melody. In the familiar-title puzzles, ordinary definitions help even when a reader does not remember the recording.
answerNotes.SUMMER: Summer scenes use familiar warm-weather outings. Actual temperatures and traditions differ between regions and families.

words: Send out water in fine drops
Faucet controlling the flow of water
Part of a circle's curved edge
Colored arc seen when sun shines through rain

answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.HOSE: A hose is a flexible tube. A nozzle shapes the flow at one end, while a tap controls its supply at the other.
answerNotes.TAP: Tap can mean a faucet or a light knock. The water-container scene uses the faucet meaning.
answerNotes.GRASS: Grass commonly covers lawns and meadows. A pasture is land where animals graze on grass and other low plants.
answerNotes.SUMMER: Summer scenes use familiar warm-weather outings. Actual temperatures and traditions differ between regions and families.
answerNotes.SPIN: Spin means rotate around a center. A top stays upright while turning quickly, then wobbles as it slows.
answerNotes.RAINBOW: A rainbow appears when light interacts with water drops. Its curved colored bands are a light effect, not a solid object.

answerNotes.SWING: Swing can name a hanging seat or the action of moving a bat. The porch and ballpark settings point to different meanings.
answerNotes.CHAIN: A chain is made from connected links. On a porch swing it provides support; on a bicycle it transfers motion.
answerNotes.PORCH: A porch is an outdoor entrance area, often with a roof. A patio is usually a paved sitting area at ground level.
answerNotes.SHADE: Shade blocks direct sunlight. A shaded garden corner still receives some light; it is different from a completely dark room.
answerNotes.SUMMER: Summer scenes use familiar warm-weather outings. Actual temperatures and traditions differ between regions and families.

focus: The setting is a Bowl of Watermelon Wedges. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Large juicy summer fruit often served in wedges
Piece of fruit cut wider at one edge
Plant part from which a new plant grows
Sweet produce such as an apple
Thin flat piece cut from food
Warmest season in most U.S. states

answerNotes.WEDGE: A wedge narrows toward one edge or point. A lemon wedge and a cheese wedge share that shape but are different foods.
answerNotes.GREEN: Green describes many growing leaves. It is also a color name in its own right, so read whether the clue asks for a plant or its appearance.
answerNotes.SEED: A seed contains the beginning of a new plant. A seed packet's planting instructions describe how to help it start growing.
answerNotes.JUICE: Juice is liquid released from fruit or vegetables. Pulp is the soft plant material that may remain mixed into it.
answerNotes.SWEET: Sweet describes flavor, not temperature or texture. A food can be sweet and cold, or sweet and warm.
answerNotes.FRUIT: Everyday fruit dishes can mix several kinds of plant produce. The serving word is culinary and does not require a botanical classification.
answerNotes.BOWL: A bowl has raised curved sides. That shape helps hold liquid or contain a mixture while it is stirred.
answerNotes.SLICE: A slice is a flat cut portion of food. Slice can also be the action of cutting food into those portions.
answerNotes.SUMMER: Summer scenes use familiar warm-weather outings. Actual temperatures and traditions differ between regions and families.
